issues.failure_explanation: The preceding bound contains the denominator 1-(\alpha) and both C^{1-(\alpha)} and C^{-(1-(\alpha))} terms, whereas the displayed proof step replaces 1-(\alpha) by 1-\alpha, inserts a factor \alpha into the numerator, and then factors the result as \aleph^\alpha\max\{1,C^\alpha\} times the maximum prefactor. For noninteger \alpha>1, 1-\alpha is negative while 1-(\alpha) is positive, so the asserted equality does not follow; the C-dependence also is not controlled by the stated factorization.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the combination of the truncation, polynomial-approximation, and quadrature errors while retaining 1-(\alpha), correcting the C^{1-(\alpha)} numerator factor, and absorbing only fixed \alpha,\beta,\sigma,C-dependent constants into the \mathcal{O} terms or the prefactor; the root-exponential rates can be preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem \ref{mainthm} does not establish the stated error bound as written. The later generalization to g(z)z^\alpha and the corner-domain theorem, which build on this theorem, are unreliable until the algebra is repaired.
issues.title: Invalid error factorization in the proof of the main z^alpha theorem
issues.why_classification: The defect is in the proof's algebra rather than in the advertised rate, and a contained re-estimation with corrected constants should recover the same theorem; no new global architecture or loss of the root-exponential regime is required.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed factored expression is not implied by the preceding bound: the bound contains \kappa^2T terms, mixed powers C^{\alpha-m-1}, and a separate coefficient involving \sin(\alpha\pi)\log C and \cos(\alpha\pi) that is not shown to be controlled by \aleph^\alpha\max\{1,C^\alpha\}/(\alpha{\cal X}(\beta)). For fixed \alpha,\beta,\sigma,C such constants can be absorbed, but the proof asserts the factorization without the needed estimates.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing fixed-parameter constant estimates for the \kappa^2T, C^{\alpha-m-1}, and \sin(\alpha\pi)\log C+\alpha\pi\cos(\alpha\pi) terms, then convert T=\sigma\alpha\sqrt{N_1} to \sqrt{N} as in the z^\alpha case; the stated \sqrt{N} and integer-\alpha regimes should remain intact.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem \ref{mainthm2}'s proof is incomplete at the final estimation step, and the logarithmic part of Theorem \ref{mainthmG} and the logarithmic corner bounds in Theorem \ref{corner} inherit that gap.
issues.title: Unjustified factoring of the logarithmic-case error bound
issues.why_classification: Only a contained final-estimation repair is needed and the advertised convergence regimes are expected to survive; the issue does not force abandonment of the theorem or a change in its rate.

issues.failure_explanation: If r_N(w)=\sum_j a_j/(w-p_j)+P(w), then r_N(x^2)=\sum_j a_j/((x-\widetilde p_j)(x+\widetilde p_j))+P(x^2) for \widetilde p_j=i\sqrt{C}\,e^{-\frac{\sigma}{2}(\sqrt{N_1}-\sqrt j)}. Thus the composed approximant has pole set \{\pm\widetilde p_j\}, whereas the corollary identifies its poles only with the single branch \widetilde p_j defined in \eqref{eq:1taperedimag}. The error identities for the composed function are still meaningful, but the stated pole construction is incomplete.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The constant $\mathcal{O}(1)$ in \eqref{asy0000}  is independent of $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\sigma$, $n$, $T$  and $z\in S_\beta'$ too.

issues.failure_explanation: For \beta\not=0 the Chebyshev parameters give \omega=1/2, so the retained factor (2\omega^{-1})^{m-1}=4^{m-1} grows faster than \aleph^m=3^m. Replacing \mathbb{T}_{m,\beta} by \aleph^m while keeping that factor does not yield an \mathcal{O}(1) constant independent of \alpha,\beta,\sigma. The T-asymptotic residue bounds used by the quadrature theorem remain valid for fixed \alpha,\beta,\sigma if m-dependent constants are allowed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either enlarge \aleph for \beta\not=0 to dominate (\delta+\omega+3/2)(2/\omega), or delete the claim of independence from \alpha,\beta,\sigma and allow the implied constants to depend on these fixed parameters.
issues.overall_effect: Only the proof's stronger uniformity assertion is false; the e^{-T} and e^{-\eta^2T} residue rates needed for fixed parameters are not lost.
issues.title: Residue proof claims parameter-independent constants that the Chebyshev-node estimate does not support
issues.why_classification: This is a constant-uniformity overclaim with a routine repair and no change to the root-exponential conclusions relied on by the later theorems.

issues.failure_explanation: The domain has vertices w_1,\ldots,w_\ell, but the unified parameter \beta is defined with \max_{1\le k\le m}\beta_k, introducing the undefined index m. Moreover, if \mathfrak{K}_1=0 or \mathfrak{K}_1=\ell, one of \alpha',\alpha'' is a minimum over an empty set, so the displayed alternative rate is not defined for homogeneous power-only or log-only corner configurations.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace m by \ell in \beta=\max_{1\le k\le \ell}\beta_k, and either adopt the convention that a minimum over an empty set is +\infty or split the theorem into mixed, pure-power, and pure-log cases.
issues.overall_effect: The unified-rate statement in Theorem \ref{corner} is ill-defined at the index level and for homogeneous corner-type edge cases, although the mixed-corner case and the per-corner rates remain meaningful.
issues.title: Unified corner parameters use an undefined index and empty minima
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local statement-level correction using a standard empty-minimum convention or a case split; it does not alter the proved per-corner rates or the mixed-corner conclusion.
